elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about my nationality, origin, language, and city.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Nice to meet you!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: More about me
- Materials: World map, flag cards, profile template, COSYmanuals 'to be' and 'articles' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• state nationality, origin, and city of residence
• use capital letters for countries and languages
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles introductions and 'to be' from Lesson 1.

Next lesson: Lesson 3 recycles family vocabulary in a cultural-exchange context.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

france — a country in Europe. Example: I come from France.
french — the language of France. Example: I speak French.
england — a country in the UK. Example: She lives in England.
english — the language of England. Example: We are learning English.
country — a nation with its own government. Example: Which country are you from?
come from — to have your origin in a place. Example: I come from Egypt.
nationality — the country you belong to. Example: What is your nationality?
language — a system of words people speak. Example: English is a world language.
city — a large town. Example: Cairo is a big city.
live — to have your home in a place. Example: I live in Cairo.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I come from... (stating origin)
• I live in... (stating residence)
• I speak... (stating language)
• My nationality is... (stating nationality)
• Where are you from? (asking about origin)
• What language do you speak? (asking about language)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a country in Europe'?
Which word means 'the language of France'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Country and language stress; capital letters in writing

France /frɑːns/ — one syllable
French /frentʃ/ — ends with /tʃ/
England /ˈɪŋɡlənd/ — stress the first syllable
nationality /ˌnæʃəˈnæləti/ — stress the third syllable
Listen and repeat:
I come from France. I live in Paris. I speak French and English.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be' to say who someone is, how they feel, and where they are from.

Form:
The verb 'to be': I am / You are / He, she, it is / We are / They are. Negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't. Question: Am I...? Are you...? Is he...?

Examples:
• I am a student.
• She is from Spain.
• We are happy today.
• They are not teachers.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My name ___ Alex.
They ___ from Italy.
I ___ tired today.
She ___ not a teacher.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am ... (a student / happy / from Egypt).
• She is ... (a teacher / tired / from Spain).
• They are ... (students / at home / happy).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
• Is she from France? — Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
• Are they happy? — Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write two true sentences with 'I am...' and 'I am not...'.
• Introduce two people in the class with 'He/She is...'.
Reading: More about me

I come from France and I live in Paris. I speak French and English. My nationality is French. Paris is a beautiful city. My friend comes from England. She lives in London and speaks English. We are from different countries, but we are good friends. Where are you from? What language do you speak?
Where does the writer live?
What language does the friend speak?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Where are you from?
B: I come from France, but I live in England.
A: What language do you speak?
B: I speak French and English.
A: What is your nationality?
B: I am French.
Where does the speaker live?
What is the speaker's nationality?
Speaking task: Create a personal profile card with your country, city, nationality, and languages. Present it to your partner.

• Where are you from?
• Where do you live now?
• What languages do you speak?
• What is your nationality?
• Which country would you like to visit?
Role-play: You are at an international student welcome event. Introduce your background and ask three people about theirs.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a personal profile (5–6 sentences) about your origin, city, nationality, and languages.
Model: I come from ... I live in ... I speak ... My nationality is ...
